body.p: The Applicant appreciates the Examiner's thorough examination of the subject application.
The Examiner rejects claims 27-47 under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph as allegedly being indefinite.
As shown in the Amendments to the Claims above, the Applicant has amended claim 27 to traverse the Examiner's rejection.
Accordingly, claims 27-47 are definite and in accordance with 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph.

The Examiner rejects claims 1-4, 15-18, 24, 27-30 and 40-43 under 35 U.S.C. 103 as allegedly being unpatentable in view of Manseur et al. (U.S. Patent No. 5,816,245). The Examiner also rejects claims 5 and 31 under 35 U.S.C. 103 as allegedly being unpatentable in view of Manseur et al. and Stoddard et (U.S. Pub. No. 2008/0269577. The Examiner also rejects claims 7-11, 19-23, 33-37, and 44-47 under 35 U.S.C. 103 as allegedly being unpatentable in view of Manseur et al. and Stoddart et al in view of McCoy (U.S. Pub. No 2013/0018240). The Examiner also rejects claim 14 under 35 U.S.C. 103 as allegedly being unpatentable in view of Manseur et al. and Stoddart et al in view of Kannan et al. ("A computational model to detect and quantify a primary blast lung injury using near-infrared optical tomography").
The Applicant appreciates and thanks the Examiner for indicating claims 25 and 26
would be allowable if rewritten in independent form including all the features of the base claim and any intervening claims.

In response, the Applicant has amended independent claim 1 to include the features of allowable claim 25 and intervening claim 24. The Applicant has also amended corresponding method claim 27 to include similar features.
Accordingly, the Applicant believes the application is now in condition for allowance.

Each of the Examiner's rejections has been addressed or traversed. It is respectfully submitted that the application is in condition for allowance. Early and favorable action is respectfully requested.

If for any reason this Response is found to be incomplete, or if at any time it appears that a telephone conference with counsel would help advance prosecution, please telephone the undersigned or his associates, collect in Peabody, Massachusetts at (781) 890-5678.
